payingUser: A working colourist - self-employed, chair-renting or employed - who buys their own reference tools rather than using the salon's booking software.
paidUnit: One non-consumable unlock of the full formula book: unlimited clients, the complete per-client visit history and exportable client colour cards.
momentOfPayment: After the colourist has entered their third client and taps to add a fourth, or taps Export on a client card; the first three clients are free and fully functional.
distinctnessSentence: A brand-agnostic formula book the colourist owns, which reproduces the exact shades and developer ratio used on a returning client without an account, a brand catalogue or a network.
day1RevenuePath: A colourist finds it in the store search for a colour formula app, records three clients free, taps to add a fourth, and buys the 9.99 dollar unlock through Play Billing.
assumptionsUnverified: That a colourist pays 9.99 dollars once rather than keeping the salon's paper colour cards; the only on-shelf evidence of a paid mechanism is the IAP badge on an independent competitor at 10K+ installs and 40 reviews, which shows a mechanism exists and not that it earns.

That one-time in-app-purchase conversion lands in the 1 to 3 percent band used in the arithmetic; that band is carried from docs/monetization-strategy.md section 4, which labels it UNVERIFIED, so it is not a measurement of this niche.

That the two recent independent attempts at this exact job - one showing a 0+ install bucket and one at 10+ installs - failed on distribution rather than on the job being unwanted; nothing measured here separates those two causes.

That the professional sub-shelf has no weak rated incumbent to displace at all, since its only two rated apps sit at 4.4 stars; the recipe therefore rests on a content gap rather than on a badly built competitor.
